newsitem.title: USA: Apple sees smaller operating loss in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Apple sees smaller operating loss in Q3.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc Wednesday said it expects to see higher revenues and a reduced operating loss in the third quarter as its restructuring program takes hold.

"We expect to see rapid improvements in the company's financial performance as the results of restructuring kick in," Apple chief financial officer Fred Anderson said in a statement. "We anticipate higher revenues and a significantly reduced operating loss in the company's third fiscal quarter and continued progress toward our goal of returning to profitability in the fourth quarter."

As reported, Apple posted a loss in the second quarter ended March 28 of $708 million, or $5.64 a share, compared with a net loss of $740 million or $5.99 per share, in the year-ago quarter. Exclusive of a $155 million restructuring charge and a charge of $375 million for the purchase of NeXT Software Inc, Apple's current second quarter operating loss was $186 million or $1.48 a share.
According to First Call, analysts had expected Apple to post an operating loss of $1.22 a share.
Revenues for the quarter were $1.6 billion, compared to $2.2 billion in the year ago quarter.
Apple said international sales accounted for 49 percent of total revenues in the current quarter.
Gross margins for the second quarter were 19 percent, compared to nine percent before inventory adjustments in the year-ago quarter.
"While the operating results are disappointing, we made significant progress toward executing our strategic plans during the quarter," Apple chairman and chief executive officer Gilbert Amelio said.
"We've streamlined our organization and narrowed our focus, we're divesting non-core assets, and we're executing a plan to reduce annual operating expenses by $500 million," Amelio said.

Anderson said Apple's cash balance at the end of the second quarter was in excess of $1.4 billion, inventories were just over $500 million, and despite the quarter's loss, Apple generated positive cash flow from operations.

Apple said Claris Corp, Apple's wholly-owned software subsidiary, achieved revenues of $70 million during the quarter. The company said revenue growth was driven in large part by an unprecedented level of operating system upgrades to Mac Operating System 7.6, introduced in January.
